title: Affine étale schemes lift across closed immersions into affine schemes
statement: Let X, Z, V be schemes [def-pc-scheme], X and V affine, i : Z → X a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and p : V → Z étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. There exists an affine scheme U with an étale q : U → X and a : V → U making the square (a,p,q,i) a fiber product [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Stacks Tag 09ZA, proof, first paragraph; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZA

proof.text: Compose i with X.isoSpec.hom. IsClosedImmersion.Spec_iff supplies an ideal I of Γ(X, ⊤), an isomorphism eZ : Z ≅ Spec(Γ(X, ⊤)/I), and the factorization of i. Write V as Spec Γ(V, ⊤) using V.isoSpec and use Spec.map_surjective to express eV.inv ≫ p ≫ eZ.hom as Spec.map f. HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff identifies its étaleness with that of f.

source.place: Stacks Tag 09ZA, proof, first paragraph; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZA

proof.text: Apply Algebra.exists_etale_coefficientLift to f.hom.toAlgebra. Its explicit Jacobian lift C has an étale algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) C and a reduction L.reduction, with a ring equivalence e : C/IC ≃+* Γ(V, ⊤) agreeing with L.reduction after the quotient map. Compose the inverse of quotIdealMapEquivTensorQuot with e to obtain E : C ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] (Γ(X, ⊤)/I) ≃+* Γ(V, ⊤). On c ⊗ 1 this equals L.reduction c. Evaluate polynomialReduction on constants to show L.reduction(algebraMap r) = f(mk I r). Quotient surjectivity and the tensor balancing identity establish the second structural-map compatibility. Transport CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct along E to give a pushout with arrows algebraMap, mk I, L.reduction and f.

source.place: Stacks Tag 09ZA, proof, first paragraph; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZA

proof.text: Apply isPullback_SpecMap_of_isPushout to the constructed ring square. Set U = Spec C, q = Spec.map(algebraMap) ≫ X.isoSpec.inv, and a = eV.hom ≫ Spec.map(L.reduction). The Spec étale criterion and composition with an isomorphism show q is étale. IsPullback.of_iso' transports the square using eV, the identity of U, eZ, and X.isoSpec; its four compatibility equations follow from the definitions, Spec.map_surjective, and the factorization of i.
